transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-06
Time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Recording: auto (Fireflies)
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Ravi Menon (Redwood SE), Jules Kim (Redwood Solutions), Evan Morales (Aurora Head of Partnerships), Priya Rao (Aurora Cloud Solutions), Ben Chu (Aurora Lead Infra)

Summary:
Quick partner intro between Redwood and Aurora Compute to explore integration touchpoints: dedicated capacity + marketplace listing, private (VPC) deployments for regulated customers, and a pilot to validate throughput/latency on H100/A100. Action items agreed for docs, pilot architecture, and a SE deep dive next week.

Topics:
- High-level partnership goals and GTM motion
- Technical integration: hosting modes (hosted API vs dedicated vs private VPC), VPC peering, onboarding process
- Performance / benchmarking: expected QPS, preferred GPUs, batching, KV cache behavior
- Security & compliance: SOC2, SAML/SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Pilot scope and next steps

Action items (captured in notes): see metadata for owners/due dates

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Sofia from Redwood, AE on the partnership team. Quick round robin?
[00:10] Evan Morales: Hey Sofia, Evan here, Head of Partnerships at Aurora. Excited to talk.
[00:16] Priya Rao: Priya, Cloud Solutions. I'll be the tech hookup today.
[00:19] Ben Chu: Ben, infra. Happy to dig into networking and perf.
[00:24] Ravi Menon: Ravi from Redwood, SE. I'll lead the technical deep dive and pilot plan.
[00:28] Jules Kim: Jules from Solutions — I'll follow up on the partner program details.

[01:05] Sofia Patel: Cool. High level, Redwood provides inference runtime across hosted, dedicated and private deployments. We're looking to partner with Aurora to list an integrated offering in your marketplace and to enable dedicated capacity / private installs for joint customers. Wanted to understand Aurora's priorities and typical customer constraints.
[01:22] Evan Morales: Yeah the short version, Aurora's getting more inbound from enterprise customers who want a one-stop for GPU infra + managed inference. They ask about isolation, certified stack, and sometimes on-prem. So partnership with a serving runtime that does batch and low-latency is attractive.
[01:35] Priya Rao: We have customers on H100 clusters and some on A100. They care about predictable latency for chat use cases, and cost controls for embeddings workloads. Networking-wise we can do VPC peering or private link.
[01:50] Ben Chu: Also want to understand what level of telemetry / tracing Redwood exposes — we need to map to our observability.

[02:30] Ravi Menon: Right. On Redwood side we do token-level latency and cost breakdowns, tracing hooks per route, and we support audit logs + integrations with external observability via OTLP. I'll send a short doc after, but we can demo the tracing in the SE call.
[02:47] Evan Morales: Nice, do you support customer-managed KMS? Some customers mandate owning keys.
[02:54] Sofia Patel: Yes, in Private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM integrations. For Dedicated we can also integrate KMS depending on the contract.

[03:20] Priya Rao: On the deployment model — how do you handle model variants? We have both open-models and some customers that want commercial models.
[03:28] Ravi Menon: We have a model catalog and runtime routing policies; we can pin model versions, do canary rollouts, and fallback to compatible variants. For commercial models the licensing is typically handled in parallel — we'd need to confirm vendor terms, but from runtime perspective we can host many model families and do quantized variants.

[04:01] Ben Chu: What about autoscaling and burst capacity on Dedicated? Do you have control plane hooks for scheduling?
[04:08] Sofia Patel: Yes, Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity; we expose metrics and a control API. There is a small delay on spin-up if we need to allocate more GPUs but we can offer burst pools for predictable throughput.

[05:00] Evan Morales: That's helpful. A lot of enterprise asks are around isolation and compliance — SOC2, ISO, SSO, RBAC. Do you have those in place?
[05:10] Jules Kim: Redwood is SOC2 compliant, we have SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit logs. We'll share the security pack after the call.
[05:19] Priya Rao: Good. For networking we'll need specifics on endpoints, whether you support VPC peering vs private link, and firewall rules.
[05:29] Ravi Menon: We support VPC peering and, for Private installs, full customer-managed control plane. For hosted + dedicated we can provide PrivateLink in some regions. I'll list the IP ranges and ports in the follow-up.

[06:15] Ben Chu: On performance — do you do KV cache / prefix caching? That's important for chat workloads.
[06:22] Ravi Menon: Yes, we have KV cache management and automatic prefix caching. There might be slight differences depending on model and quantization profile, but we've tuned for high throughput. Also continuous batching helps reduce per-token cost.
[06:38] Priya Rao: How are multitenancy and noisy neighbor handled on dedicated pools?
[06:45] Sofia Patel: Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools so noisy neighbor risk is minimal; we also have scheduling and priority lanes if needed.

[08:00] Evan Morales: Let's talk about a pilot. Ideally Aurora wants a joint pilot that validates both performance and integration flow so we can promote on the marketplace. What's a realistic pilot scope?
[08:12] Ravi Menon: Typical pilot: 2-4 weeks, validate throughput and tail latency on representative prompts, test VPC peering and telemetry, and verify billing/metrics integration. For GPUs we can run on your H100 nodes or supply Redwood's staging dedicated capacity — whichever preferred.
[08:30] Ben Chu: We prefer running on our clusters (H100) to show customers the experience. We'll need clear ops runbook to spin up containers / runtime.
[08:37] Ravi Menon: Great — we'll prepare a pilot architecture diagram. We'll need a small test dataset and some representative prompt patterns to emulate chat + embeddings.

[09:20] Priya Rao: On billing and pricing, how does Dedicated partner pricing work? Do you have reseller margins or marketplace revenue share models?
[09:27] Sofia Patel: We have a partner program with a few options: marketplace listing with revenue share, reseller with committed capacity discounts, or joint go-to-market credits. Jules will follow up with the partner sheet.
[09:40] Jules Kim: Yup will send the partner program doc and sample contract language.

[11:05] Evan Morales: A couple of tricky asks we get: customers wanting air-gapped/on-prem installs; and some with strict data residency. Can Redwood support on-prem packages?
[11:14] Ravi Menon: We do offer a Private on-prem package for regulated customers — customer-managed control plane and optional air-gapped deployments. There are extra operational costs but it's supported.
[11:26] Ben Chu: For the on-prem option, what are the minimum hardware requirements?
[11:30] Ravi Menon: We'll send a spec but roughly we require at least N GPUs (depends on model) and a control plane node; for H100 we recommend X TB of NVMe and 1 Gbps interconnects for small setups, higher for scale. I'll include concrete numbers in the follow-up so Ben can review.

[13:00] Priya Rao: Any pitfalls you've seen with customers during VPC peering? We want to avoid long config cycles.
[13:07] Ravi Menon: Biggest thing is routing and security groups — we provide a step-by-step template and sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippets to speed it up. Also sometimes MTU and long-lived sockets need tuning for large KV caches.

[15:15] Evan Morales: On SLA and uptime, do you offer enterprise SLAs for Dedicated?
[15:22] Sofia Patel: Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. We can discuss specific numbers depending on the committed capacity and region.

[16:40] Ben Chu: For model variants and quantized weights — do you control quantization or is that something we need to do?
[16:47] Ravi Menon: Our runtime supports multiple quantization profiles and we can recommend which profile to use per workload. We also handle kernel selection and some compilation optimizations on deploy. For new models we typically work with the partner to validate quality/regression.

[18:05] Priya Rao: Can Redwood integrate with our billing system or do we rely solely on Redwood invoices?
[18:12] Sofia Patel: We have flexible billing — resale, marketplace integration, and APIs for usage metrics so you can reconcile. We'll include example endpoints for pulling usage metrics.

[20:00] Evan Morales: Competitor question — some partners run their own inference stacks or resell other solutions. What should we highlight that differentiates Redwood?
[20:10] Sofia Patel: Emphasize production-first runtime (low latency, batching, smart routing), unified experience across hosted/dedicated/private, and cost controls via batching/quantization recommendations. Also our rollout tooling (canary, automatic fallback) is a differentiator.

[22:30] Ben Chu: We'll need to run a benchmark. Can you propose a minimal benchmark plan?
[22:36] Ravi Menon: Sure — proposed plan: 1) define 3 representative prompt sets (chat short, chat long, embeddings), 2) run steady-state QPS tests for 15 minutes each, 3) capture p50/p95/p99 latencies and token cost, 4) test warm/cold KV cache scenarios. We'll share a spreadsheet template.

[24:05] Priya Rao: Note: Some customers require SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning. Do you support SCIM?
[24:12] Jules Kim: Yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync. We'll include the SAML metadata and SCIM endpoints in the pack.

[26:00] Evan Morales: Great. On marketplace listing, what assets do you need from Aurora?
[26:06] Jules Kim: Logo, short description, one-pager, and any compliance badges. Also we like a small joint case study or reference if available. We'll send the marketplace onboarding checklist.

[28:10] Ben Chu: Any compliance limitations for running commercial LLMs in Private deployments?
[28:17] Ravi Menon: As long as licensing permits local hosting, Private deployments are fine. For cloud-hosted commercial models we need to check vendor T&Cs. We'll help validate.

[30:00] Sofia Patel: Let's capture next steps: we'll send partner pack and security docs, Ravi prepares pilot architecture and bench template, and Evan will share KPIs. Then schedule SE deep dive next week.
[30:12] Evan Morales: Sounds good.

[31:00] Priya Rao: Quick question — is there a sandbox or staging account we can use for initial integration?
[31:07] Sofia Patel: Yes we can provision a trial test tenant for Aurora. It will have restricted capacity for early testing. We'll include credentials in the secure email.

[33:00] Ben Chu: For telemetry and tracing — can we export traces to our OTLP collector?
[33:07] Ravi Menon: Yes, we support OTLP export and also provide logs/audit records. We'll add the config snippet.

[35:20] Evan Morales: Ok that's the bulk. Anything else from Redwood?
[35:25] Sofia Patel: Nothing more. We'll follow up with docs and align calendar invites for the SE deep dive. Thanks everyone.
[35:33] Priya Rao: Thanks all.
[35:36] Jules Kim: Thanks, bye.

(Recording ends)
